industrious

in-DUS-tree-us -- from Latin industria ('diligence, activity'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Industrious is consistently hardworking and diligent.

The industrious beekeeper checked every hive by hand twice a week, rain or shine.

Example

While her roommates slept in every Saturday, the industrious grad student was already three hours into her thesis by nine a.m.

That steady, self-driven work ethic -- showing up and putting in effort day after day without being told to -- is exactly what industrious describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

productive: Productive measures output — a productive meeting is one where a lot got decided, whoever or whatever moved things along. Industrious describes the person instead: a steady, self-driven habit of working hard day after day. An industrious student can still have a slow, fruitless day; the trait is effort, not results.

hardworking: Hardworking simply praises the effort someone puts in on a given job. Industrious goes further: it names a settled, self-starting habit — the industrious person seeks out work steadily, day after day, without being told. One demanding week can make you hardworking; industrious describes what you are like all year.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

idle: not working or active

slothful: habitually lazy

Where it sits · how unending the effort is — dedicated → industrious → tireless

dedicated vs. industrious: Dedicated is milder than industrious: a dedicated student turns his homework in a day early, while an industrious one works hard at everything, steadily and without letting up.

tireless vs. industrious: Tireless is stronger than industrious: an industrious worker puts in steady effort all day and then rests, while a tireless one never seems to need rest at all, pressing on hour after hour without flagging.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — industri-

root — industri-: diligence, activity (Latin (industria))

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin (-osus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin industria meant 'diligence, activity,' and adding -ous ('full of') describes a person full of that diligent energy. The same root gives us industry, though industrious describes a person's hardworking character rather than a factory or trade.

Use the root in a new word: industrial

Use the root in a new word: industrial: The city's old industrial district has slowly been converted into apartments and art studios.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Industrious describes a person's own steady, self-motivated work ethic -- it's a warmer, more personal word than 'productive,' which just describes the results.
